text: The changed L11 manifest blocks of `ac` (fsu38c8q), `dto` (xvm9aann), `endpoint` (vc5pzsc0), `design-system` (dsmanifest) and `ui-view` (cv8b7alf) list, inside the frontend module that now enters through the browser entry, `editorExtensions — [<type>SlashCommand]` and a `sidebarTab.order` (ac 5, dto 3, endpoint 2, design-system 6, ui-view 5). Both values are carried over unchanged from the `before_change` block — they are not this window's change. The code has, since earlier releases, deliberately NO `editorExtensions` slash command on those modules: each envelope declares its trigger once, in `contributes.commands` (carrying the `popoverKind` the host dispatches on); a second module-borne entry is exactly the trap the database-tables page (91vq520g) describes — the palette matches both, picks the module one, which carries no popover discriminator, and opens nothing. Sidebar orders/displayOrder in code are ac 50, endpoint 10, dto 20, ui-view 40, design-system 60, database-table 100, mcp-tool 8. Assumed: the window's change (frontend out of `EntityContribution`, into a module registered by the browser entry) is built; the slot list is honoured except `editorExtensions` on these five types and the sidebar order numbers, which stay as they are (adding the slash extensions would reintroduce the dead palette entry; renumbering the ELEMENTS order is a user-visible product choice not made by this window). The `[section:…]` tests do not assert `editorExtensions` or `order` values for these types. Suggestion for the spec: drop `editorExtensions` from those five module comments (as the database-table page already does, naming `contributes.commands` as the only declaration) and align the order numbers with the code, or say which numbers are intended.
assumption: ASSUMPTION:dev-2004 — the five visible package types keep NO `editorExtensions` slash command (the trigger lives only in `contributes.commands`) and keep their current sidebar order numbers; only the move of the frontend out of the contribution is built.
